name: Ripple USD
who_can_redeem: Ripple describes RLUSD as redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars. User terms distinguish general users from customers and make detailed redemption availability dependent on eligibility, supported jurisdictions, compliance controls, network support, and current Ripple terms.
redemption_region_notes: RLUSD availability is jurisdiction-dependent. SOG separates Ripple issuer redemption, supported platform access, XRP Ledger / Ethereum deployment, exchange liquidity, and secondary-market trading.
redemption_notes: PR-028A separates RLUSD issuer overview, transparency reports, legal terms, developer docs, and implementation references. The record should not imply universal retail redemption without terms-level review.
summary: USD-backed stablecoin issued by Ripple. SOG records RLUSD as active with cash-equivalent reserve framing, monthly reserve attestation archive context, jurisdiction-dependent access, NYDFS/DFSA context, BNY custody reference, and XRP Ledger / Ethereum deployment notes as separate source-backed layers.
notes: Deepened in PR-028A. Evidence now includes Ripple issuer page, reserve transparency page, legal terms, developer docs, and implementation repository. Exact period-level attestation entries, customer redemption requirements, and final deployment identifiers remain source-review areas.

name: EURC
who_can_redeem: Circle describes EURC as redeemable 1:1 for euro and supported by Circle Mint for business access. Retail and jurisdictional availability should be reviewed separately.
redemption_region_notes: Circle describes EURC as MiCA-compliant and available on supported chains; availability depends on account type, region, and Circle terms.
redemption_notes: SOG separates EURC issuer redemption and Circle Mint conversion from exchange liquidity, DeFi use, and cross-chain movement.
summary: Euro-backed stablecoin issued by Circle. SOG records EURC as active, with MiCA, reserve, monthly attestation, Circle Mint, and multichain context as source-backed layers.

name: Pax Dollar
who_can_redeem: Paxos describes USDP as redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars. Direct minting and redemption availability depends on Paxos account eligibility, current terms, jurisdiction, and customer onboarding.
redemption_region_notes: SOG separates Paxos issuer redemption, Ethereum and Solana deployment references, exchange liquidity, and secondary-market trading. Exact customer access and regional eligibility still require terms-level review.
redemption_notes: PR-028C separates USDP issuer overview, Paxos transparency entry point, Ethereum contract reference, Solana token reference, and implementation repository. Final redemption availability should not be inferred from market liquidity alone.
summary: USD-backed stablecoin issued by Paxos. SOG records USDP as active with NYDFS oversight context, cash-equivalent reserve framing, 1:1 redemption framing, Paxos reserve report entry point, and Ethereum / Solana deployment references as separate source-backed layers.
notes: Deepened in PR-028C. Evidence now includes Paxos USDP page, Paxos transparency entry point, Ethereum explorer reference, Solana explorer reference, and Paxos contract repository. Period-level reserve reports, current redemption terms, and Solana lifecycle status remain source-review areas.

name: Global Dollar
who_can_redeem: Global Dollar Network describes USDG as fully backed and redeemable from Paxos on a one-to-one basis for U.S. dollars. SOG keeps direct issuer redemption, network-mediated access, partner access, and exchange liquidity separate.
redemption_region_notes: USDG involves Global Dollar Network and Paxos-related issuer context. Jurisdiction, issuer entity, partner access, and customer eligibility remain source-review areas until separated by durable sources.
redemption_notes: PR-028D separates USDG network overview, Paxos issuer entry point, reserve entry points, redemption path, network partner context, and chain/deployment unknowns. Do not treat network participation, exchange support, or partner incentives as issuer redemption without source review.
summary: USD-backed stablecoin associated with Global Dollar Network and Paxos-related issuer entities. SOG records USDG as active with network structure, issuer-entity questions, reserve disclosure entry points, redemption path, partner-network context, and unresolved deployment identifiers as separate source-backed layers.
notes: Deepened in PR-028D. Evidence now includes Global Dollar Network page, Paxos USDG entry point, and network documentation entry point. Issuer entity, period-level reserve reports, direct redemption path, partner roles, and supported chain identifiers remain source-review areas.

name: USDS
who_can_redeem: USDS is part of the Sky Protocol ecosystem. Access generally occurs through protocol or interface flows rather than a fiat-backed issuer redemption model. DAI-to-USDS conversion, USDS-to-sUSDS savings flows, protocol exits, and secondary-market access should be treated separately.
redemption_region_notes: Sky.money is a non-custodial interface and does not control or guarantee protocol rates. Interface availability, protocol availability, DAI/USDS conversion, sUSDS access, and chain-specific deployment should be recorded as separate layers.
redemption_notes: PR-028E separates USDS stablecoin status from DAI upgrade or conversion context, sUSDS savings-token context, Sky Savings Rate, protocol governance, collateral composition, bridge/deployment context, and interface availability. A fiat-reserve redemption model is not applied to USDS.
summary: Protocol stablecoin associated with the MakerDAO / Sky transition. SOG records USDS as active with DAI-to-USDS lifecycle context, sUSDS and Sky Savings Rate as related but separate product layers, protocol-based collateral and exit mechanics, governance-dependent rates, and unresolved chain/contract details as source-backed or source-review fields.
notes: Deepened in PR-028E. Evidence now includes Sky.money, the sUSDS page, Sky developer docs, Sky Ecosystem GitHub, and the Sky info dashboard. DAI/USDS upgrade mechanics, exact collateral composition, rates and governance history, interface restrictions, bridge status, and final contract addresses remain source-review areas.
